Written by the DSL course sync from templates/site/ in the # toolkit; every sync rewrites it. layout: page --- {{ content }} {% comment %} Your Profile - the settings that let every other page offer a file in the student's own copy (see _includes/open_in.html, which owns the URL rules and is included below so that this page's own buttons derive a path exactly the way a file row does). One static page, no back end: the site is public and identical for everybody, so what it learns here it keeps in the reader's own browser (localStorage) and sends nowhere. Nothing is stored until a Save is pressed, and every button below step 1 reads the SAVED values, not what is currently in a box - a half-typed path that enabled a button would open the wrong folder and look like the page's fault. One Save per field, beside its own box, with what it stored on the line underneath. On a save the box empties and the value it stored becomes the box's placeholder, so the field shows its setting the way an unfilled field shows its example. That is also why an empty box plus Save is a no-op rather than a delete: the box is empty after every save, and the second press must not wipe what the first one stored. `clear` on the saved line is how a setting is actually removed. Four numbered steps, in the order they have to happen: details, fork, clone, open. Step 3 stays greyed until step 2 has been taken, because cloning a fork that does not exist yet is the one failure mode with no useful error at the other end - the editor just reports a repository it cannot find. "Mark this step done" is the way out for a student who forked last term, or on another machine: the flag is this browser's, not GitHub's, and the page cannot ask GitHub without sending the reader's handle somewhere. The materials repo is named once here, as the default a cohort release deploys into (`cohort_dest_repo`, dsl_course/deploy.py). Nothing else on this page depends on it: the per-file control reads the repo out of each file's own GitHub URL, so a course that renamed its materials repo still gets working file links and only these buttons point at the default name. {% endcomment %}

1 Your details

Your GitHub username - the last part of your profile address.

Where your clone of materials is, or the folder you are about to clone it into.

Where your assignment repos sit. Blank means the same folder as above.

Editor

Your editor's link scheme, ending in {path} where the file goes. The separator before it belongs to the scheme, as in the VS Code one (vscode://file/{path}).

2 Fork the materials repo

Your own copy on GitHub, where your notes and your edits are yours to keep.

Fork materials Already forked it, or forked it on another machine? Mark this step done. Forked - step 3 is unlocked.

3 Clone your fork

Brings the whole repo down into your materials folder.

Clone your fork Save a GitHub handle in step 1 to enable this. Fork the repo in step 2 to enable this.

4 Open it in your editor

Open your cloned fork locally Save a materials folder in step 1, and an editor link ending /{path}, to enable this.
